title: Finite free tensor reduction for a finitely generated field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $K/k$ and $L/k$ be field extensions [def-pc-field-extension], and assume $K=k(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ for finitely many elements of $K$, where this denotes the smallest subfield containing $k$ and these elements. There exist $r\geq0$ and elements $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in K$ forming a transcendence basis [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], a subfield $F=k(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\subset K$, an integer $d\geq1$, and an $F$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $K$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. For these choices put $A=F\otimes_kL$ and $T=K\otimes_kL$ with algebra tensor multiplication [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and give $T$ its $A$-algebra structure by $f\otimes l\mapsto f\otimes l$. The map $A\otimes_FK\to T$, $(f\otimes l)\otimes u\mapsto fu\otimes l$, is an $A$-algebra isomorphism. The map $A^d\to T$, $(c_i)\mapsto\sum_i c_i(e_i\otimes1)$, is an $A$-linear isomorphism. In particular $T$ is finite free over $A$, and $A\to T$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and integral [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. No separability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM), proof: choose a finite extension of a purely transcendental extension and form its finite free tensor map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis] to $K/k$ and put $F=k(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$. Thus $K/F$ is algebraic. Also $F(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=K$: this field contains $k$ and all the $a_i$, and is contained in $K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] over $F$ to these same generators. It gives a finite spanning list for $K$ over $F$. Successively discard any vector in the span of the others; the resulting finite list still spans and is linearly independent, since a nonzero coefficient in a dependence over a field would express its vector in terms of the others. This is a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ by [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Since $1\ne0$ in $K$, an empty list cannot span, so $d\ge1$.

source.place: Tags 030F (lemma-transcendence-degree), 09GH (lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated); unpacking the finite extension in Tag 045M.

proof.text: Use the bilinearity universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The formula $((f\otimes l),u)\mapsto fu\otimes l$ is $F$-balanced: multiplying either $f$ or $u$ by $h\in F$ gives $fhu\otimes l$; it also respects the inner $k$-relations. It therefore gives $\alpha:A\otimes_FK\to T$. Conversely $(u,l)\mapsto(1\otimes l)\otimes u$ is $k$-balanced, since $(1\otimes bl)\otimes u=(b\otimes l)\otimes u=(1\otimes l)\otimes bu$ for $b\in k$. It gives $\beta:T\to A\otimes_FK$. On generators, $\alpha\beta(u\otimes l)=u\otimes l$ and $\beta\alpha((f\otimes l)\otimes u)=(1\otimes l)\otimes fu=(f\otimes l)\otimes u$. Thus they are inverse additive maps. Tensor multiplication gives $\alpha(((f\otimes l)\otimes u)((g\otimes m)\otimes v))=fguv\otimes lm=(fu\otimes l)(gv\otimes m)$, and $\alpha(1)=1$. Moreover $\alpha((f\otimes l)\otimes1)=f\otimes l$, so $\alpha$ respects the specified $A$-algebra structure.

source.place: Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM), finite purely transcendental subfield and finite free tensor map in its proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-base-change-free] to the ring map $F\to A$, $f\mapsto f\otimes1$, and the basis just chosen. The vectors $1_A\otimes e_i$ form an $A$-basis of $A\otimes_FK$. The $A$-linear isomorphism $\alpha$ sends them to $e_i\otimes1$, so these form a basis of $T$. By the basis definition [def-weil-pbc-free-module], its coordinate map is precisely $A^d\to T$, $(c_i)\mapsto\sum_i c_i(e_i\otimes1)$; this proves the claimed finite freeness.

source.place: Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM), finite purely transcendental subfield and finite free tensor map in its proof.

proof.text: The finite free $A$-module $T$ is flat by [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat]. By [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], this means the specified ring map $A\to T$ is flat. The displayed finite basis also generates $T$ over $A$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] makes this ring map integral. None of these applications assumes separability.
